hints: Focus on shape as well as bond polarity, because polar bonds can cancel out if they point in opposite directions.
Notice that two of these molecules are perfectly symmetrical, so their bond dipoles add to zero despite having polar bonds.
For the two unsymmetrical molecules left, compare how strongly the dipoles pull in the same direction, remembering that C=O is very polar.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes an overall dipole**

A molecule is polar overall only if it has polar bonds AND they do not cancel by symmetry. Think of bond dipoles as little arrows pulling toward the more electronegative atom.

Rule: net dipole = vector sum of bond dipoles

**Eliminate the symmetrical molecules**

Molecule A is $\text{C}_2\text{Cl}_4$. The $\text{C-Cl}$ dipoles are arranged symmetrically around the $\text{C=C}$ bond, so they cancel. Molecule D is $\text{O=C=O}$, which is linear, so the two $\text{C=O}$ dipoles pull equally opposite and cancel.

$$\text{A: symmetrical alkene, net = 0}$$
$$\text{D: O} \leftarrow \text{C} \rightarrow \text{O, net = 0}$$

**Compare the two polar carbonyl molecules**

Molecule B is $\text{H}_2\text{C=O}$ (methanal) and molecule C is $\text{Cl}_2\text{C=O}$ (phosgene). Both are trigonal planar and unsymmetrical, so both have a net dipole pointing toward the oxygen.

$$\text{C}^{\delta+} - \text{O}^{\delta-} \text{ is the dominant dipole}$$

**Decide which net dipole is largest**

In B, the $\text{C-H}$ bonds are almost non-polar, so almost the full $\text{C=O}$ dipole is felt. In C, the two $\text{C-Cl}$ dipoles pull partly upward, opposing the $\text{C=O}$ dipole and reducing the net result. So B keeps the largest overall dipole.

options.A: Incorrect. Although each C-Cl bond is polar, the molecule C2Cl4 is symmetrical about the C=C bond. The four dipoles cancel in pairs, giving zero overall dipole.
options.B: Correct. Methanal, H2C=O, has a very polar C=O bond and two almost non-polar C-H bonds in a trigonal planar shape. There is nothing to cancel the C=O dipole, so it shows the largest net dipole of the four.
options.C: Incorrect. Phosgene, Cl2C=O, is polar, but the two polar C-Cl bonds have a component that pulls against the C=O bond. This partial cancellation makes its net dipole smaller than that of methanal.
options.D: Incorrect. Carbon dioxide, O=C=O, has two very polar C=O bonds but is linear and symmetrical. The dipoles are equal and opposite, so they cancel completely to give zero overall dipole.
